newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares up sharply in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares up sharply in early trading.

text.p: Israeli share prices opened the week sharply higher on Sunday and analysts attributed the rise to a clutch of good news over the weekend.
In early afternoon trading, the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's Mishtanim index of 100 leading shares was up 2.20 percent to 291.19 after the market opened on strong demand. Shares rose across the board.
"There's renewed interest in buying stocks. The whole atmosphere is bullish," said Jonathan Ross, vice president of Nesuah Securities. "The market is happy."

Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities, said the rise was in part due to news that Merrill Lynch had acquired 19 percent of drug maker Agis Industries Ltd for 200 million shekels for distribution to clients.

In addition, Doron said, newspaper reports said Britain's Cable and Wireless had bought up 11 million shekels of Bezeq Israel Telecom shares in the market. Cable controls about 10 percent of state-owned Bezeq and has been seeking an agreement with the Israeli government over its future role in the company.
Tsur also noted the record high for the Dow Jones Industrial Index on Friday as well as news of the resumption of negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.

However, the talks, due to begin in Cairo on Sunday, were put on hold after the sides squabbled over Palestinian reports Israel had agreed to a "pause" in building Jewish settlements in exchange for renewing the talks.
Ross said the market was inclined to shrug off political developments.
"I don't think the political situation should give people confidence," he said. "But it hasn't affected sentiment in the marketplace."
He said the market was moved mainly by improved corporate profits and low valuations. He noted that after adjusting for inflation, the Mishtanim index had not reached its 1994 peak.
Except for a pause from mid-Feberuary to mid-April, the Mishtanim has been rising steadily since October 1996. Since the start of this year, the index has risen in excess of 35 percent.
